content: When using this medication, it is essential to use a barrier method of contraception, such as condoms or a diaphragm, every time you engage in sexual activity until your next menstrual period occurs. If you are currently using or planning to use hormonal birth control, you must wait at least five days after taking this medication before starting hormonal contraception. This is because the interaction between these medications can reduce the effectiveness of both. Once you begin hormonal birth control, continue using a barrier method of contraception during sexual activity until your next menstrual period. Common side effects of this medication may include headache, nausea, abdominal pain, fatigue, dizziness, or painful menstrual periods. It is important to remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they have determined that the benefits to you outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. If you are in Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Before taking ulipristal, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to progestins (such as levonorgestrel or norethindrone), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other complications. This medication may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you are confident you can do so safely. Limit your intake of alcoholic beverages. This medication must not be used during pregnancy. It can pass into breast milk, and due to potential risks to the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended while using this drug. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain medications may reduce the effectiveness of emergency contraception, potentially leading to pregnancy. Examples include griseofulvin, modafinil, rifamycins (such as rifampin or rifabutin), and St. John’s Wort. Overdose with this medication is highly unlikely. However, if someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. For further information, consult your healthcare professional.
